summary: The core is laid out as the GX631 board: each instance is named after its board location (u16A, u11A, u12D, u11F, u14F, u1H, u8H...) and connected pin to pin, with custom-chip modules for the 007343 PAL, the 007327 palette RAM/DAC and the 005885 video chip. The video pipeline latches data on H/V counter bit edges and scans pixel by pixel, sprites go through a double-buffered line buffer, and the two 005885 colour outputs are merged in glue logic. None of this resembles MAME's tilemap and gfx draw_sprites_region structure. MAME carries over little beyond the memory map and register semantics that any correct core must share.

findings.note: The top level instantiates parts by reference designator (u16A/u11A 6809s, u12D 007343, u11F/u14F 005885s, u14B shared RAM, u8H/u7H/u12H/u13H mask ROMs, u9H/u14H PROMs, u1H 007327, u8C YM2151) and wires them by their pins. It has no MAME-like driver state class.

Main-CPU decode is written as PAL equations over A4..A13, A8_9 (A8|A9), WR, OBJB, GATEB and GATECS, producing MGCS/SGCS/IOCS/CRCS. MAME instead uses address-map ranges with memory_view/bank switching (m_videoview, m_spritebank).
The sprite bank and 005885 select bits drive the PAL's OBJB/GATEB inputs, which steer chip selects between the two 005885s. MAME's rambank_w swaps memory banks and views in software.

The palette is two 8-bit RAM halves split by A0/NA0, with an address mux selected by SEL between the colour bus CB and the CPU bus, plus BLK blanking and a pixel latch on CEN. MAME uses palette_device indirect pens built from the PROM.

findings.signal: Palette write strobe from E/Q latch
findings.note: The palette write enable comes from a flip-flop clocked by the 6809's Q and cleared by E & ~RW, and RA[11:8] is muxed between the CPU and the colour bus. MAME does not model this board-level timing.

findings.signal: Two-chip colour merge in glue logic
findings.note: The 8bpp background comes from combining the two 005885 COL[4:0] outputs (color_sel = both COL[4], with the nibbles concatenated) plus a blank term. MAME's approach is a single 8bpp gfx_layout spanning both ROM halves.

The tile attribute, code and ROM data are latched on rising and falling edges of h_cnt[2] and h_cnt[1]. Fine scroll is applied with a 32-bit shift register and nibble select, and zram addresses come from the scrolled position bits. MAME instead builds a 32x32 tilemap and sets scroll rows/cols.

findings.signal: External H4 latch for attribute bits
findings.note: VRAM D4/D5 are taken out through the ATR4/ATR5 pins and latched on both edges of an H4 derived from the 005885 H1O. They become graphics ROM address bits. MAME computes the same bits arithmetically as ((attr&0x30)<<6).

findings.signal: Scanline sprite engine with line buffer
findings.note: Each scanline, an FSM walks 5-byte entries and renders into a double-buffered line buffer (bank = vpos[0]) with transparent-skip writes. Sprite size is decoded from ly/lx bits. MAME's per-sprite half-size branches (spritenum*4, mod=-8, multiple DRAW_SPRITE calls) do not appear. The engine was adapted from another core, not from MAME.

The core models bootleg PCB behaviour that MAME does not (shifted HBlank, a missing last sprite line, blacked-out edge columns, no blank signal). It does this by changing counter compare points and blank conditions, as the hardware would.
The register layout (scroll y/x, scroll_ctrl row/col modes, tile_ctrl bit 3 sprite buffer, flip/irq bits) matches MAME's semantics. Any correct core has to share these.

findings.signal: FPGA clocking and SDRAM tile fetch
findings.note: The clock enables from 49.152 MHz, the E/Q phase generator, the fractional divider for the YM2151 and the SDRAM time-multiplexing of the two tile ROMs are FPGA engineering choices.
